prompt_text:
Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that handles partial and final streaming recognition events using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 4 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 5 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 6 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
import wave

import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

def stream_audio_file_to_text(audio_file_path: str):
    """
    Streams an audio file to the Azure Speech-to-Text service and prints
    partial and final recognition results.
    """
    # This example requires environment variables AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
<GAP>
    speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(
        subscription=os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY"),
        region=os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_REGION")
    )
    speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"

    audio_config = speechsdk.AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=False) # We will provide audio from a file

    # Create a push audio input stream
    push_stream = speechsdk.audio.PushAudioInputStream()
    audio_config = speechsdk.AudioConfig(stream=push_stream)

    speech_recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(
        speech_config=speech_config,
        audio_config=audio_config
    )

    # Connect callbacks for partial and final results
    speech_recognizer.recognizing.connect(
        lambda evt: print(f"RECOGNIZING: {evt.result.text}")
    )
    speech_recognizer.recognized.connect(
        lambda evt: print(f"RECOGNIZED: {evt.result.text}")
    )
    speech_recognizer.session_started.connect(
        lambda evt: print(f"Session started: {evt}")
    )
    speech_recognizer.session_stopped.connect(
        lambda evt: print(f"Session stopped: {evt}")
    )
    speech_recognizer.canceled.connect(
        lambda evt: print(f"CANCELED: Reason={evt.reason}; ErrorDetails={evt.error_details}")
    )

    # Start continuous recognition in a separate thread/task
    speech_recognizer.start_continuous_recognition_async()

    # Read the audio file and push it to the stream
    with wave.open(audio_file_path, 'rb') as wf:
        # Assuming 16-bit PCM, 16000 Hz, 1 channel as commonly used with Azure STT
        # Adjust these if your audio file has different properties
        if not (wf.getframerate() == 16000 and wf.getsampwidth() == 2 and wf.getnchannels() == 1):
            raise ValueError("Audio file must be 16kHz, 16-bit, mono PCM WAV.")

        chunk_size = 1024 # bytes
        while True:
            frames = wf.readframes(chunk_size // wf.getsampwidth())
            if not frames:
                break
            push_stream.write(frames)
            # Simulate real-time by adding a small delay
            # await asyncio.sleep(len(frames) / (wf.getframerate() * wf.getsampwidth() * wf.getnchannels()))
            
    # Signal the end of the audio stream
    push_stream.close()

    # Wait for recognition to complete (or for a certain duration)
    # In a real application, you might use an event to signal completion
    # or a more sophisticated loop. For this example, we'll just wait a bit.
    print("End of audio stream. Waiting for final results...")
    asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(asyncio.sleep(5)) # Give it some time to process
    
    speech_recognizer.stop_continuous_recognition_async()

    print("Recognition process finished.")
